rounds.user:
Customer email from Harbor & Finch:

“Hi Noor — we were charged for 12 seats last month, but only 10 were in use. Could you refund the two unused seats? Thanks, Maya.”

Pull the relevant refund clause from policy.md and tell me how it applies here.
rounds.assistant: policy.md says subscription charges are non-refundable once a billing period begins, including charges for unused seats. Under the written policy, Harbor & Finch is not entitled to a refund for the two seats, though you could make a discretionary exception.

rounds.user: I’ll make a one-time exception as an account credit, not a cash refund. Draft a short reply to Maya that states the policy without sounding defensive and offers credit for the two unused seats.
rounds.assistant:
Subject: Re: Unused seats

Hi Maya — our policy normally treats subscription charges as non-refundable once the billing period starts, including unused seats. That said, I’m happy to make a one-time exception and apply a credit for the two unused seats to your next invoice. I’ll confirm once the credit is applied.

Best,
Noor

rounds.user: Next: Northwind Logistics wants the liability cap in their annual contract raised from 1× to 3× annual fees. Draft a replacement limitation-of-liability clause at 3×, keeping the rest of the clause structure intact.
rounds.assistant: Here is a replacement clause preserving the existing structure while raising the aggregate liability cap to three times the annual fees paid or payable under the agreement. It retains the existing exclusions for indirect and consequential damages.

rounds.user: Revise the Northwind clause to cap liability at 2× annual fees instead. Add a carve-out so the cap does not apply to liability arising from a data breach caused by our failure to meet the agreement’s security obligations.
rounds.assistant: Revised: aggregate liability is capped at two times the annual fees paid or payable, except that the cap does not apply to liability arising from a data breach caused by a party’s failure to comply with its security obligations under the agreement. The existing exclusion of indirect and consequential damages remains unchanged.

rounds.user: Keep the 2× cap and the data-breach carve-out. Add a 12-month notice term for any change to those liability terms, and give me the full revised clause.
rounds.assistant: Revised clause: aggregate liability is capped at two times the annual fees paid or payable, except for liability arising from a data breach caused by failure to meet the agreement’s security obligations. The existing exclusion of indirect and consequential damages remains. Neither party may amend these liability terms without at least 12 months’ prior written notice.

rounds.user: Back to Northwind. Their lawyer accepts the 2× annual-fees cap and the data-breach carve-out, but wants 6 months’ notice instead of 12. I’m willing to settle at 9 months. Draft the final full clause with the 9-month notice term.
rounds.assistant: Final clause: Except for liability arising from a data breach caused by a party’s failure to comply with its security obligations under this Agreement, each party’s aggregate liability under or relating to this Agreement will not exceed two times the annual fees paid or payable under it. The existing exclusion of indirect and consequential damages remains in effect. Neither party may amend these liability terms without at least nine months’ prior written notice.

rounds.user: Back to Harbor & Finch. Maya replied: “Thanks, that works. Can we also remove the two unused seats going forward?” Draft a brief reply confirming I’ll reduce them from 12 to 10 seats starting next billing cycle and confirm the change by Friday.
rounds.assistant:

Best,
Noor
